newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end down on labour uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end down on labour uncertainty.

text.p: South Korean stocks slipped on Wednesday in weak trading as uncertainty over a controversial labour law continued to sour sentiment, brokers said.
They also blamed weakening fundamentals, such as falling customer deposits at brokerage houses.

The composite stock index lost 11.60 points to close at a provisional 678.94. "Investors began to worry about the damage the labour unrest has caused. In addition, weakening market fundamentals must have dented sentiment," said Kim Heung-shik of Hyundai Securities. Brokers said they expected a record trade deficit in January because of the labour trouble.
Strikes cost 2.85 trillion won in lost production and $509 million in lost exports, the trade ministry figures showed.
Brokers said a downward correction was anticipated after about 20 percent gains in the index over the past two weeks.

They said customer deposits began to fall since Monday from this year's high of 2.93 trillion won and interest rates rose because of prospects of heavy new three-year corporate bond issues in February.
Volume totalled 36.68 million shares, compared with 44.3 million on Tuesday. Decliners outpaced advancers 567 to 227 with 112 unchanged.
